summary.text: Debbie Wasserman Schultz is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Florida's 20th District, first sworn into the House in 2005, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

Before Congress she served eight years in the Florida House and four in the Florida Senate; she chaired the Democratic National Committee from 2011 to 2016 and serves on the House Appropriations Committee.

paragraphs.text: Wasserman Schultz was born in Queens, New York, in 1966 and graduated from Half Hollow Hills High School East in 1984.

She attended the University of Florida, where her official biography says she was president of the Student Senate, and earned a bachelor's degree in 1988 and a master's degree in 1990, both in political science.
Before running for office she worked as a staffer to U.S. Representative Peter Deutsch (D).
She served in the Florida House of Representatives from 1992 to 2000 and in the Florida Senate from 2000 to 2004.
She was first sworn into the U.S. House in 2005, and her official biography describes her as Florida's first Jewish congresswoman.
From 2011 to 2016 she chaired the Democratic National Committee.
Wasserman Schultz serves on the House Appropriations Committee, with seats on the Agriculture, Energy and Water, and Military Construction and Veterans Affairs subcommittees in the 119th Congress.

Her official biography says she was the first woman to chair the Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Subcommittee, in the 117th Congress, and that she co-chairs the Democratic Steering and Policy Committee in the 119th Congress.

That biography also lists legislation she authored or sponsored, including the Virginia Graeme Baker Pool and Spa Safety Act (2007), the PROTECT Our Children Act (2007), the EARLY Act (enacted in 2010 as part of the Affordable Care Act) and the Rape Survivor Child Custody Act (signed in 2015).
She advanced from the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary for the 20th District.
According to her official biography, she is married to Steve Schultz and they have three children.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election with 74.4% of the vote to Brent Andersen's 21.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
